root_cause.text: The mt7921 AP path accepted unvalidated station AID values in `mt7921_mac_sta_add()` and `mt7921_mac_sta_event()`, allowing AIDs above the firmware’s supported limit to be passed to the firmware and trigger a crash.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (sta->aid > MT7921_MAX_AID) return -ENOENT;` in both functions and defines `MT7921_MAX_AID 20`, while the CVE states that “Any station configured with an AID over 20 causes a firmware crash” on IFTYPE_AP interfaces.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (sta->aid > MT7921_MAX_AID) return -ENOENT;` in both functions and defines `MT7921_MAX_AID 20`, while the CVE states that “Any station configured with an AID over 20 causes a firmware crash” on IFTYPE_AP interfaces.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject station entries with out-of-range AID values before allocating resources.
intent_record.what: A new bounds check was added at the start of mt7921_mac_sta_add(): if sta->aid is greater than MT7921_MAX_AID, the function now returns -ENOENT before attempting WCID allocation.
intent_record.how: This prevents station addition from proceeding with an AID value outside the supported range, avoiding invalid state setup and later allocation/lookup failures by rejecting the station early.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an AID range check to reject invalid station events before association handling.
intent_record.what: A bounds check was added at the start of mt7921_mac_sta_event(): if sta->aid is greater than MT7921_MAX_AID, the function now returns -ENOENT before continuing; the existing association-event check remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now rejects station events with an association ID outside the supported range, preventing further processing for invalid AIDs and avoiding any downstream handling that assumes a valid station index.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a named MT7921 maximum AID constant for use in driver logic.
intent_record.what: A new preprocessor macro `MT7921_MAX_AID` was added with the value `20` near the existing MT7921 ring size definitions.
intent_record.how: This introduces a named constant that can be used elsewhere in the code to cap or reference the maximum AID value for MT7921, making any such limit explicit and centralized.

consistency_review.core_intent: Reject invalid station events by checking that AID values are within range before association handling or resource allocation.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they add AID range validation in the AP station add/event paths to reject out-of-range AIDs before passing them on, preventing the firmware crash.

The change introduces a dedicated MT7921 maximum AID constant, which directly relates to the root cause of unvalidated AID handling in the AP path. Defining the limit is part of constraining AID values before passing them to firmware.

candidates.rationale: This allocation path is part of station setup that previously lacked an AID upper-bound check; an out-of-range AID could proceed through association handling and resource allocation toward firmware.
This is the association-event gate in mt7921_mac_sta_event(); before the fix, no AID validation occurred after this point, so invalid AIDs were accepted during assoc handling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This station setup path allocated a WCID without any preceding upper-bound validation of the station AID, allowing out-of-range AIDs to continue into firmware-facing association handling.

This is the association-event branch point in mt7921_mac_sta_event(); before the fix, no AID range check occurred here, so invalid AIDs could be accepted and passed onward to firmware during association.
